description.narrative: The overall objective of the project called FUTURE Developing green driven society and sustainable environmental CSOs in Bosnia and Herzegovina is to strengthen environmental governance by building the capacity and empowerment of environmental civil society organizations (ECSOs) and networks to effectively participate in the national and regional agenda for environment as change agents in advocating and influencing environmental policy development and implementation for better natural resource management and environmental protection. The FUTURE project will built upon results achieved within the recently closed NEST project, implemented by REC since 2021. The specific objectives of the project are: To build capacities, increase knowledge and technical background of ECSOs which will enable them to become a valued partners and transformative/change agents in environmental governance able to effectively advocate and contribute to policy development for main environmental challenges from local to national levels as well as to contribute to EU integration and negotiations processes in BIH. To enhance organizational capacities of ECOs and enabling platform for improvement of government accountability, environmental transparency and environmental governance. To improve management and effectiveness of the existing protected areas through strengthening cooperation and dialogue with ESCOs and thus create preconditions for expansion of protected areas network and establishment of new protected area. To strengthen professional capacities of judiciary and law enforcement officials for processing the most complex environmental cases and implementation of EU Environmental crimes legislation, as one of the basic preconditions on the path towards European integration. To improve multiagency networking established within the NEST project through experience and best practices exchange with other organizations and networks (INTERPOL, IMPEL, EUFJE and ENPE) in order to support BiH for ensuring effective transposition, harmonization, implementation and enforcement of EU environmental laws.

Att stärka miljöstyrningen genom att bygga upp kapaciteten och bemyndigandet hos miljöorganisationer inom det civila samhället och nätverk för att effektivt delta i den nationella och regionala agendan för miljön som förändringsagenter i att förespråka och påverka utveckling och genomförande av miljöpolitik för bättre naturresursförvaltning och miljö skydd.

To strengthen environmental governance by building the capacity and empowerment of environmental civil society organizations and networks to effectively participate in the national and regional agenda for environment as change agents in advocating and influencing environmental policy development and implementation for better natural resource management and environmental protection.

Overall, the project has made significant progress, delivering a range of activities and outputs aligned with its ambitious objectives. These include the launch of organizational development grants for Environmental CSOs, completion of training needs assessments, work for the development of management plans in protected areas, work with judiciary, etc. Some activities, however, experienced delays due to administrative procedures, government approvals, and other formal requirements, particularly in the Republic of Srpska. In contrast, implementation in the Federation of BiH has advanced steadily, including the signing of cooperation agreements with cantonal ministries and preparatory engagement with protected area authorities. Throughout the 2025, adjustments were made in consultation with stakeholders to ensure that activities remain relevant, feasible, and impact-oriented, taking into account practical implementation experiences and lessons learned.
During the first year of implementation, the following key results were achieved:
Official kick of project in March 2025. Project web site and social networks developed, serving as the main information hub for beneficiaries, stakeholders and the general public.
Organizational assessment of environmental CSOs was done with an aim to examine the environment in which CSOs operate and to evaluate their capacities and needs regarding influence on environmental policy formulation and monitoring of policy implementation in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The main results were compiled into a Register of Environmental CSOs. The Register (which will be published and made available online) will serve as a comprehensive and up-to-date database of environmental civil society organizations in BiH, facilitating networking, information exchange, and partnership-building among CSOs. It will also provide relevant public institutions, donors, and other stakeholders with reliable data for consultation processes, policy dialogue, targeted capacity-building support, and more effective inclusion of civil society in environmental governance and decision-making processes.
Trainings aimed at strengthening the organizational sustainability and capacities of environmental civil society organizations were executed. Trainings specifically targeted locally active environmental CSOs that are open to improving their internal structures, legitimacy, representativeness, and professional expertise in the field of environmental protection. An in-depth Training Needs Assessment (TNA) of environmental civil society organizations awarded organizational grants was conducted as an initial step as to ensure that the upcoming trainings reflect the needs and priorities of ECSOs.
Grant component for organizational development was successfully implemented and provided financial support to enhance sixteen (16) ECSOs organizational development, internal capacities, and expertise. The support was particularly important given the limited availability of core funding for small ECSOs, enabling essential improvements in governance, legal status, membership structures, and overall organizational functioning. REC closely monitors the implementation process, providing guidance and support to grantees to ensure activities are carried out in line with approved Organizational Development Plans (ODPs) and project objectives.
Number of networking meetings with relevant ministries of environment and other non-environmental CSOs and organisations were held as to ensure coordination and best cooperation.
Manual for Organizational Development of environmental CSOs is developed providing guidance and practical solutions on Self-assessment of organizations, Organizational structure and governance, Organizational development, strategic planning and management, Financial management and sustainability, Communication, advocacy, and networking strategies. It serves as a comprehensive resource to strengthen the capacity and effectiveness of environmental CSOs in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Preparatory steps for protected areas management have been taken through the establishment of cooperation with the proposed protected areas. Engagement with relevant authorities and stakeholders has been initiated, laying the groundwork for future development of management plans, capacity-building of park staff and rangers, and long-term conservation efforts. Selection of protected areas where no management plan existed or where revision of an existing plan or development of new management plan was needed has been done in cooperation with competent ministries. FEDERATION OF BiH nominated Nature Park Hutovo Blato and Protected natural monument Skakavac, whilst REPUBLIC OF SRPSKA nominated Nature Park Praa and Nature Park Tara. However implementation on Development and/or revision of Management Planes in nominated PAs is currently delayed due to the slow and extensive administrative procedures, as well as the approval processes required by the relevant Ministries.
The Curriculum on Environmental Law for Judges and Prosecutors in BiH is prepared and sent to Centers for Judges and Prosecutors in FBiH and RS for review and comments. It is expected to be approved and adopted by the Management Boards of the Centers for Judges and Prosecutors in FBiH and RS soon.
The first training for judges and prosecutors from Bosnia and Herzegovina was held with an aim to strengthen their capacities on ACCESS TO JUSTICE IN ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION TOOLS AND MECHANISMS OF THE AARHUS CONVENTION and to secure better implementation and enforcement of the national environmental legislation in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Long-term cooperation with international networks, such as INTERPOL and IMPEL, has been initiated to provide ongoing technical support, capacity-building, and access to resources for environmental crime prevention and alignment with EU environmental legislation.
